criteria.name: Shift to bilateral missions
criteria.description: Assess the transition from multilateral peacekeeping toward bilateral deployments and how this reflects changing regional security dynamics and Rwanda’s strategic positioning.

criteria.name: Unilateral engagements and proxies
criteria.description: Evaluate the rise of unilateral operations and support to allied non-state groups, including implications for conflict escalation and regional stability.

criteria.name: Civilian impact patterns
criteria.description: Analyze how operational tactics and use of proxy forces affect civilian safety, noting trends in indirect fire, displacement, and localized protection or harm.

criteria.name: Security gap opportunism
criteria.description: Examine how Rwanda capitalizes on reduced external peacekeeping and shifting partnerships to expand its role as an alternative security provider.

criteria.name: Economic leverage and resource control
criteria.description: Investigate the pursuit of commercial benefits and control of strategic routes and resource sites linked to foreign deployments, and how this shapes motivations and outcomes.

criteria.name: Political influence in host states
criteria.description: Explore efforts to reshape local governance and political arrangements in areas of deployment, including the replacement or alignment of local authorities.

criteria.name: International legitimacy balancing
criteria.description: Consider how contributions to peacekeeping are used to counter external criticism of other operations, and the strategic trade-offs in maintaining international support.

criteria.name: Narratives of security justification
criteria.description: Assess official rationales for interventions, such as cross-border threats and identity protection claims, and how these narratives are contested by critics.

criteria.name: Regional power dynamics
criteria.description: Evaluate how Rwanda’s expanding military footprint alters alliances, rivalries, and the broader geopolitical balance in the Great Lakes and surrounding regions.

criteria.name: Operational effectiveness and limits
criteria.description: Review evidence of success in countering armed groups and reducing violence in targeted areas, alongside limitations in curbing abuses by other actors.

criteria.name: Military professionalization and training gains
criteria.description: Analyze how foreign deployments contribute to tactical experience, force readiness, and institutional capacity, and how these gains feed back into national strategy.

criteria.name: Risk of escalation and spillover
criteria.description: Identify trends indicating potential widening of conflicts due to external support, heavy weapon use, or cross-border operations, and their regional repercussions.

criteria.name: Private sector-party linkages
criteria.description: Examine connections between deployments and firms affiliated with ruling elites, assessing how party-owned enterprises benefit and influence policy choices.

criteria.name: Information denial and attribution
criteria.description: Assess patterns in official denials versus emerging evidence from field reporting and imagery, and the implications for transparency and accountability.

criteria.name: Host government reception
criteria.description: Evaluate the mixed responses from partner governments to Rwandan deployments, including acceptance, skepticism, and conditions affecting cooperation.
